title: Placement and portability decision model
description: Compare three workload contracts against three placement models. The model separates a reusable operating surface from state, network, identity, and provider capabilities that still need an explicit home.
assumptions: Illustrative planning model, not a provider quote or benchmark. Changed-state volume, WAN round-trip time, and the eight-layer portability inventory are visible so a team can replace them with measured values before approving a design.

workloads.label: EU order ledger
workloads.detail: Critical writes need one authority, EU data residency, a recovery copy, and a tested 30-minute recovery path.
requirements: Customer records remain in approved EU locations
One write authority protects order and payment invariants
Recovery point stays within five minutes

workloads.label: Global media API
workloads.detail: Large immutable objects should serve near users while metadata writes retain one clear authority.
requirements: Media reads stay off the metadata write path
Object copies have an owner and retention policy
Metadata writes remain idempotent during retries
Cross-cloud transfer is measured by source and destination

workloads.label: Private inference gateway
workloads.detail: Raw features remain on premises; sanitized jobs may burst to cloud GPUs when local capacity is exhausted.
requirements: Raw features never leave the private boundary
Only policy-approved derived payloads may burst
Local inference remains available when the WAN fails
Cloud jobs have bounded queues and deletion evidence

strategies.label: Uniform stack everywhere
strategies.detail: Recreate every tier in each domain and coordinate state across providers.

layers.label: Runtime
layers.note: The same image and workload contract run in each cluster.

layers.label: Traffic
layers.note: Health, DNS, load balancing, certificates, and routes differ by provider.

layers.label: State
layers.note: A common database engine still needs a WAN consistency and recovery model.

layers.label: Operations
layers.note: Shared telemetry semantics feed separate quotas, incidents, and billing exports.

regulated-ledger.summary: A synchronous cross-cloud write path spends latency and partition tolerance without creating a safe two-site quorum.
regulated-ledger.decision: Keep the ledger authority in one approved failure domain and build a separately tested recovery path. Revisit multi-writer state only when the product invariant and conflict model require it.

checks.label: EU residency
checks.detail: All modeled state copies can be restricted to approved EU locations.

checks.label: Single write authority
checks.detail: The strategy coordinates writes across providers instead of preserving one authority.

checks.label: Partition behavior
checks.detail: A two-site synchronous dependency cannot keep accepting safe writes after the link splits.

checks.label: Recovery evidence
checks.detail: Multiple copies exist, but promotion and restore still need independent tests.

global-media.summary: Portable stateless tiers help, but copying every object and metadata change multiplies transfer and lifecycle work.
global-media.decision: Use this model only for objects that need a second provider. Serve immutable media through caches and keep the metadata authority out of the user read path.

checks.label: Read locality
checks.detail: Traffic can reach a nearby serving tier in each domain.

checks.label: Metadata authority
checks.detail: The placement does not identify one authoritative metadata write path.

checks.label: Transfer ownership
checks.detail: Two modeled remote copies move 1,800 GiB/day before retries or catch-up.

checks.label: Provider exit
checks.detail: Images and data formats are reusable, assuming copy time has been measured.

private-inference.summary: Replicating the full stack conflicts with the rule that raw features stay inside the private boundary.
private-inference.decision: Keep feature retrieval and the default inference path on premises. Export only a policy-approved derived job when cloud burst capacity is needed.

checks.label: Private feature boundary
checks.detail: The uniform model assumes state is copied to remote domains.

checks.label: WAN-independent service
checks.detail: A WAN round trip sits on the modeled critical path.

checks.label: Reusable runtime
checks.detail: The same inference image can run against provider-neutral interfaces.

checks.label: Deletion evidence
checks.detail: Three state domains increase the evidence and retention surface.

strategies.label: Portable compute, anchored state
strategies.detail: Keep one state authority; reuse images, policy, and recovery artifacts in a second domain.

layers.label: Runtime
layers.note: The image, health contract, resource envelope, and deployment intent are reused.

layers.label: Traffic
layers.note: Global routing changes only after the recovery target is promoted and verified.

layers.label: State
layers.note: Backups or an asynchronous copy move off-path with an explicit recovery point.

layers.label: Operations
layers.note: SLOs, telemetry names, policy tests, and runbooks remain common.

regulated-ledger.summary: The critical write remains local to one authority while a recovery copy moves asynchronously to an approved target.
regulated-ledger.decision: Approve only after restore, replica promotion, routing, credential access, and data-integrity checks meet the stated five-minute RPO and 30-minute RTO.

checks.label: EU residency
checks.detail: The authority and recovery target are both constrained to approved EU locations.

checks.label: Single write authority
checks.detail: The user write path reaches one authoritative ledger.

checks.label: Partition behavior
checks.detail: Interconnect loss creates replication backlog but does not split the write authority.

checks.label: Recovery evidence
checks.detail: The design exposes a promotion gate that can be tested against RPO and RTO.

global-media.summary: One metadata authority and object origin can coexist with portable serving tiers and selected recovery copies.
global-media.decision: Keep media delivery near users through caches. Replicate only objects and metadata required by the recovery or provider-exit objective.

checks.label: Read locality
checks.detail: Serving tiers and caches can remain close to users without owning metadata writes.

checks.label: Metadata authority
checks.detail: One path owns media metadata and idempotent update rules.

checks.label: Transfer ownership
checks.detail: The model exposes 900 GiB/day of changed data before compression, retries, or cache fill.

checks.label: Provider exit
checks.detail: A warm target and object inventory make copy duration and missing capabilities testable.

private-inference.summary: The private site stays authoritative and serves the default path; cloud capacity remains an optional bounded target.
private-inference.decision: Use a redaction or feature-release gate before burst jobs leave the site. The local queue and inference path must continue when cloud connectivity fails.

checks.label: Private feature boundary
checks.detail: Raw features remain in the on-premises state authority.

checks.label: WAN-independent service
checks.detail: The default inference path adds no cross-cloud round trip.

checks.label: Reusable runtime
checks.detail: Approved model images and resource contracts can target local or cloud GPU pools.

checks.label: Deletion evidence
checks.detail: Only released job payloads enter the cloud retention and deletion scope.

strategies.label: Split by capability
strategies.detail: Anchor each bounded capability where it has a clear advantage and connect them through explicit contracts.

layers.label: Runtime
layers.note: Only shared services use a common image; specialized tiers use provider-native interfaces.

layers.label: Traffic
layers.note: Versioned APIs and events keep cross-domain calls explicit and measurable.

layers.label: State
layers.note: Each dataset has one owner, export format, retention rule, and recovery target.

layers.label: Operations
layers.note: Shared SLO and trace semantics sit above provider-specific health and quota signals.

regulated-ledger.summary: Keeping the ledger anchored can work, but optional fraud, analytics, or reporting services create new data-release boundaries.
regulated-ledger.decision: Approve each export separately. Keep authorization and payment completion independent from a remote optional capability, and define deletion and replay behavior.

checks.label: EU residency
checks.detail: Every state-owning capability can be restricted to an approved EU location.

checks.label: Single write authority
checks.detail: The order ledger remains authoritative.

checks.label: Partition behavior
checks.detail: Optional remote capabilities consume events and do not block the ledger write.

checks.label: Recovery evidence
checks.detail: Three capability domains require coordinated replay and deletion drills.

global-media.summary: Media serving, transcoding, metadata, and analytics have different scaling and locality needs that can justify separate homes.
global-media.decision: Keep contracts asynchronous where the user path permits. Record which derived artifacts may be rebuilt and which originals need independent recovery copies.

checks.label: Read locality
checks.detail: Serving and cache capabilities can run independently near users.

checks.label: Metadata authority
checks.detail: The metadata capability retains one write owner.

checks.label: Transfer ownership
checks.detail: The model moves selected derivatives rather than every object copy.

checks.label: Provider exit
checks.detail: Original object formats and capability contracts define what must move during exit.

private-inference.summary: A provider GPU capability can add burst capacity, but the release boundary becomes part of the security invariant.
private-inference.decision: Require policy evidence for every exported field, cap the remote queue, and prove the private service remains useful during a prolonged WAN outage.

checks.label: Private feature boundary
checks.detail: Only approved derived payloads cross the boundary.

checks.label: WAN-independent service
checks.detail: Local inference continues while cloud burst jobs pause.

checks.label: Reusable runtime
checks.detail: Provider-native GPU queues and identity APIs need an adapter and exit test.

checks.label: Deletion evidence
checks.detail: Remote payload, logs, caches, and failed jobs need end-to-end deletion evidence.
